Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

medfit (development version)

Fixed

  • Native fits with active nonlinear constraints now use the constraint curvature in observed-information standard errors and in the observed sandwich bread. Expected-information standard errors retain their Fisher information definition. Covariance also uses the optimizer’s effective variance floors, so an active floor is pinned rather than treated as a free direction. Active inequalities and bounds give a local tangent covariance; it does not describe the full boundary sampling distribution.
  • Only explicit non-positive-definite information or negative-variance diagnostics retain an accepted likelihood through medfit_sem_covariance_error and an internal mbco_sem() null. Other covariance errors propagate unchanged. Singular information continues to warn and return an NA covariance.

Removed

  • options(medfit.native_defaults) is removed, as announced in 0.15.0. Since 0.15.0 the option had no effect (it only printed one message per session); it now does nothing and prints nothing. The message class medfit_message_option_obsolete no longer exists. Pass fixed_x and meanstructure explicitly to choose.

medfit 0.15.0

Native engine defaults flipped (0.15.0)

Behavior change for fit_sem() and fit_mediation(engine = "native"). An unset fixed_x now means the exogenous observed variables (lavaan’s fixed.x = TRUE) and an unset meanstructure now means TRUE, so a default native fit matches a default lavaan::sem() fit. This is the flip announced in 0.14.0 and in [BREAKING] #329; FALSE and NULL stay valid values, and an explicit argument is always kept as given.

  • What does not move. The structural estimates and their standard errors. The native-defaults oracle matrix (557 rows against lavaan) gives 503 pass, 54 declared limit and 0 block, the same counts as the 0.14.0 baseline; the neutrality check against 0.14.1 (explicit old defaults) differs by 0.
  • What moves. The conditional logLik() (the fixed exogenous block is no longer in the likelihood), the parameter count npar, AIC() and BIC(), and the names in coef(), vcov() and tidy() (the exogenous variances, covariances and intercepts are fixed rows, and every observed intercept is a free row). Which random start a multi-start fit tries can change, because the retry seed follows the parameter names.
  • An unset fixed_x resolves to an explicit character subset of the exogenous observed variables (glance()$fixed_x names it). A variable a ~~ or ~1 statement names is left free with a message of class medfit_message_fixed_x_lenient; an explicit fixed_x = TRUE still errors there.
  • options(medfit.native_defaults = "0.15") is obsolete: it is ignored, with one message per session (class medfit_message_option_obsolete; removed in the development version). The medfit_warning_default_change warning no longer fires.
  • To keep the 0.14.x results, pass fixed_x = FALSE, meanstructure = NULL.
  • AIC() and BIC() keep medfit’s own parameter count, which includes the observed means that are not fixed whether or not they are in the parameter vector. It equals lavaan’s count when lavaan fits the mean structure, so medfit’s AIC and BIC equal those of lavaan::sem(..., meanstructure = TRUE) under any fixed_x; a default lavaan::sem() fits no mean structure, and against it medfit’s AIC is larger by 2k and its BIC by k log n (k = the observed means not fixed; k = 2 in the worked example of the article). The conditional logLik() equals lavaan’s.
  • Missing data stays listwise deletion; there is no missing = argument and no FIML (a 0.16.0 candidate).
  • compare_lr() runs on fits made under the new defaults. Its known limit (#320) is unchanged by the flip: on the pinned design (15 seeds by 4 cells) the lavaan run ended above medfit’s reference in 18 of 60 runs and OpenMx in 13 of 60, the same counts as before, with no mislabeled row.
  • Docs: ?fit_sem, ?fit_mediation, ?compare_lr, ?"medfit-syntax", the “Native defaults in 0.15.0” article and the guides describe the new defaults. The other articles, the book and the cookbook are updated separately.

medfit 0.14.1

Outcome ledger for native zero-product fits and MBCO

  • Every native fit, zero-product branch and mbco_sem() null now keeps a versioned outcome ledger (fit@diagnostics$ledger): a stable ID, the exact restriction, the estimation sample and likelihood domain, the optimizer’s acceptance state, the discrepancy, whether a feasible point was witnessed, covariance availability, retained warnings and messages, and the original condition. An unresolved branch is unknown, never certified infeasible, and a complete enumeration is not a global-optimum certificate.
  • No result changes. An unresolved required zero-product branch is still the medfit_error_no_convergence error and never a fit (#303); the error now carries the ledger of every required branch as $ledger, and the best surviving branch’s discrepancy as $best_survivor (diagnostic only, never a p-value). The notices of a failed branch are in the ledger; messages keep their text. The sample is stored once, on the root node. mbco_sem() keeps its unresolved result (an NA statistic, unresolved TRUE) and carries the ledger as $ledger; compare_lr()’s $reference carries it too.
  • A fit whose ledger is missing, malformed or does not describe the fit is refused by mbco_sem() with a medfit_error_ledger error (a fit made before this release must be refitted). A zero-product model whose restrictions exceed the 64-branch cap still stops with its plain error; it now carries a ledger whose enumeration state is not_enumerated.
  • mbco_sem() validates its own root ledger (the full fit and one node per tested null, in order, each tied to the returned $tests table and the settings of the refit) before returning, and refuses a malformed one with medfit_error_ledger. No result or message changes; the ledger of a failed null records se_type "model", the setting its refit used.
  • Warnings and messages raised before an error are no longer replayed on the error; they are kept in $ledger only.
  • Internal: fits hold their warnings and messages while running and replay them as condition objects, so their classes now reach the caller.

Literal zero/nonzero certificates for native zero-product fits (D2)

  • A zero-product branch whose equalities contradict by literal syntax (an explicit label == 0 with an explicit finite nonzero literal equality on the same label, as a == 0 with a == 1) is certified empty: it is kept in the ledger with the proof and an unavailable likelihood, and is not fitted. A union returns only if at least one branch resolves and every other branch resolves or is certified empty. No tolerance, solver status, bound, affine contradiction or fixed table value is a proof; a failed branch stays unknown and the fit stays the medfit_error_no_convergence error.
  • Behavior change: a direct fit whose own equalities contradict literally now stops before the optimizer with medfit_sem_infeasible, whose message (“literal zero/nonzero contradiction: constraint … is violated by …”) keeps the optimizer’s wording. The semantics are exact, with no tolerance: any finite nonzero literal contradicts zero, so a == 0 with a == 1e-9 (or 1e-12) now stops with medfit_sem_infeasible where dev returned a fit, and in a zero-product union a1 * b1 == 0 with a1 == 1e-12 now selects the b1 == 0 branch instead of the a1 == 0 branch. A union whose branches are all certified empty stops with medfit_sem_empty_union. Both are medfit_error_no_convergence errors carrying $ledger, so mbco_sem() and compare_lr() report them as unresolved.

Branch map and raw cap for native zero-product fits (D3)

  • A ledger node whose constraints hold zero-product rows now carries branch_map: the raw combination count (raw_count), the factor counts from the parser (factor_counts), a structural restriction-set ID for each raw row (raw_to_canonical) and the number of distinct sets (unique_count). Duplicate or permuted products (as a*b == 0 written twice) collapse to the same ID; no affine solving is done, so it is not an equivalence certificate. Execution is unchanged: every raw row is still fitted in the original order and ties go to the first. No result changes.
  • The 64-branch cap counts raw combinations, duplicates included, and is now checked with overflow-safe arithmetic before the branch grid is allocated, so a model with a very large product count is refused with the same error instead of exhausting memory. The refusal message prints the count without scientific notation, marks a count above 2^53 as approximate and names an overflow (overflow (Inf)); the numeric raw_count and enumeration$required are Inf on overflow. An over-cap model is refused on its raw count alone: no literal certificate is tried and nothing is fitted. Its ledger has enumeration$state = "not_enumerated" and a not_enumerated map with an unknown unique count and no raw mapping. The message text for counts of 65 to 2^31 is unchanged.
  • The map is rebuilt from each node’s own constraints when the ledger is validated, so a forged ID, count or state makes mbco_sem() refuse the fit with a medfit_error_ledger error. A fit stored by a development build that predates the map (zero-product models only) must be refitted for the same reason.

Covariance-stage evidence for native fits (D4)

  • When the optimizer accepts a native fit and the covariance stage then fails, the accepted likelihood and its context are kept as evidence in a typed error, medfit_sem_covariance_error, never a returned fit (#303). The class is a sibling of medfit_error_no_convergence, not a refinement: no optimizer failed, so the handlers that turn an optimizer failure into an unresolved result do not take it. It carries $ledger (the node, with covariance failed and the original condition in post_fit) and $partial (the accepted fit without vcov or defined); its message is the original one. A failure of any other kind (model, data, optimizer, objective, an invalid definition) is unchanged and gets no covariance certificate.
  • A zero-product union with a covariance failure in one branch stops the same way after every branch has a likelihood. The root reports the first failing branch’s evidence, in branch order, even when another branch is the minimum; the branch IDs in the ledger say which one failed. A branch that did not converge still stops the call with medfit_error_no_convergence first.
  • mbco_sem() keeps the likelihood of a refit null whose covariance stage failed, after checking that it is the null that was asked for (same rows, domain, one more restriction). The statistic and p-value are unchanged, a warning names the failure, and the node of that null records covariance = "failed" and its notices. No covariance or standard error is invented, and boundary and identification warnings stay. A fit that carries covariance-failure evidence, or a malformed payload, is refused with medfit_error_ledger.
  • No result changes. Definition values and gradients are now checked before the covariance, so an invalid definition is reported as before and not hidden by a covariance-stage error.

medfit 0.14.0

Native engine defaults change in 0.15.0

medfit 0.15.0 changes two defaults of fit_sem() and fit_mediation(engine = "native") so that a default native fit matches a default lavaan fit: fixed_x becomes the exogenous observed variables (lavaan’s fixed.x = TRUE) and meanstructure becomes TRUE. 0.14.0 changes no result; it warns and lets you opt in. The schedule: 0.14.0 warns, and 0.15.0, at least two months after 0.14.0 (the notice runs on GitHub; both stay GitHub-only releases), flips both defaults together. FALSE and NULL stay valid values in every release.

  • fit_sem() and fit_mediation(engine = "native") now warn when fixed_x or meanstructure is left unset and the model is one where its default will matter in 0.15.0 (an observed exogenous variable for fixed_x; no ~1 and no product term for meanstructure). The warning has class medfit_warning_default_change, names the argument, and is shown once per session per argument. Results are unchanged in 0.14.0. Pass the argument explicitly to keep today’s results without the warning, or set options(medfit.native_defaults = "0.15") to fit with the 0.15.0 defaults now (meanstructure = TRUE, and fixed_x set to every observed exogenous column, product and factor-dummy columns included, except those a ~~ or ~1 statement names). Variables left free that way are named on each fit in a message of class medfit_message_fixed_x_lenient (field variables), and glance()$fixed_x lists the fixed set. An explicit fixed_x = TRUE still errors on such a statement. In 0.15.0 the option is ignored.

  • What moves under the new defaults: the parameter count, logLik() (conditional on the fixed variables), AIC(), BIC(), and the names in coef(), vcov() and tidy() (the exogenous moments leave them; the intercepts join them). Structural estimates and their standard errors did not move on the cases measured (the native-defaults oracle matrix: 557 cells against lavaan or a stated oracle, 503 equal and 54 recorded limits).

  • The retry seed of a multi-start fit is derived from the parameter names, so the new parameter vector changes the random starts. A well-identified fit gives the same estimates; which start wins, and whether the start-spread warning appears, can change. The reliability gate is rerun under the new defaults before 0.15.0.

  • Dependents (packages that call fit_sem() or fit_mediation(engine = "native")): pass fixed_x and meanstructure explicitly in package code, examples and tests, so your users see neither the warning nor a change of results in 0.15.0. To silence the warning in a test, catch it by class (medfit_warning_default_change).

New features

  • compare_lr() now accepts native fits with a saturated mean structure (every intercept free) and with fixed_x (TRUE, a named subset or a lenient subset), in lavaan (#319) and in OpenMx (#321). Both were refused before. The fixed exogenous moments are passed to the engine as fixed parameters at their sample values (N denominator), so the engine fits the same model medfit does; in OpenMx a fit with a mean structure runs on the raw data of exactly the rows the fit used. This lets the comparison run on fits made under the 0.15.0 defaults. OpenMx’s default start can occasionally land above medfit’s reference; that is reported as the usual statistic-above-max warning (#320).

Bug fixes

  • Behavior change. A parameter pinned by the active set (an equality such as b == 0, or an active bound) in a native fit with a mean structure now has a standard error of exactly 0, as it already had without one. The covariance was projected in centered coordinates and mapped back, which left roundoff (about 5.6e-18) on the pinned row, so tidy() reported a z-statistic and p-value for a parameter that is not estimated; they are now NA. Code that read those rows sees NA where it saw a huge z-statistic. Free parameters’ standard errors are unchanged. The fix comes first because meanstructure = TRUE becomes the default in 0.15.0.

  • ?fit_sem described fixed_x as fixing “every covariance with another exogenous variable”. An exogenous variable that the model writes a ~~ statement on is not paired with the other exogenous variables (as in lavaan), so those covariances are 0, not fixed at their sample values. The text now says “the exogenous covariances the model contains”, and ?"medfit-syntax" states the pairing rule.

medfit 0.13.0

  • Declare the existing rlang runtime dependency used by compare_lr(), resolving the undeclared-import R CMD check warning. ## Bug fixes

  • Repair pkgdown 2.2.1’s invalid /NA script URL on generated 404 pages, preserving the inline MathJax configuration.

  • The native optimizer’s acceptance gate no longer rejects a result only because NLopt reported a roundoff-limited stop (status -4). The status is not the certificate: feasibility, stationarity and curvature still decide, and a stalled point still fails them. On some CPUs (the GitHub runner’s) the extreme-scale floor fixture of the nonlinear gate ended every correct-basin start with -4, so the only accepted start was a wrong-branch one with a likelihood ratio about 2700 too high and a single-start warning (#276). Constrained fits that previously warned “only 1 of 9 starts” on such machines now return the right optimum.

  • A roundoff-limited stop that leaves the point short of a nonlinear row along a flat direction is now restored onto the row by the Newton polish (wider reach than the ordinary polish) before the gate decides; the gate still checks the restored point (#276).

  • A restoration can no longer raise the discrepancy without limit. It was accepted whenever the gate accepted the restored point, so a feasible, stationary but worse point could stand and inflate a likelihood-ratio statistic. The rise is now capped at 4 times the first-order cost of restoring feasibility, \(|g'\delta| + \tfrac12|\delta' H_L \delta|\) with \(\delta = -M^{+}c\) the minimum-norm step back onto the active rows (the multipliers times the violation, without computing them; see the Methods and Formulas article). On the fixtures that restore, every legitimate restoration rises by 0.995 to 0.9998 of that cost, so none is refused; a restoration whose cost cannot be computed (no active row, rows of rank zero) is refused. The new restoration gate in tests/sim checks the cap with planted defects.

  • Behavior change (correctness fix): a refit or a zero-product branch that the optimizer cannot fit is now an unresolved result instead of an error or a silent answer. mbco_sem() returns a row with converged = FALSE, the failure text in a new note column and an NA statistic and p-value (never the minimum over the refits that worked), with a warning and a new unresolved element; this includes a null the constraints rule out (a > 0.3 with the null a = 0), which used to stop. A model or data error in a refit (for example the rule-9 refusal of a label constraint with products) still stops. A zero-product branch that cannot be fitted while another succeeds now stops fit_sem() with a medfit_error_no_convergence error (the message lists each failed branch and the best survivor’s discrepancy), because the best of the other branches need not be the constrained optimum and a returned fit could be used by coef(), vcov(), anova() or extract_mediation() as if it were certified. Inside mbco_sem() and compare_lr() the failure is an unresolved row or the verdict "unresolved" with reference$accepted = FALSE and reference$lr = NA, not an error. Callers that read $tests$converged (missingmed does) keep working; code that relied on mbco_sem() stopping for a failed refit must check $unresolved.

medfit 0.12.0

New features

  • New compare_lr() (#249) runs the product-null likelihood-ratio test (a*b == 0) in lavaan or OpenMx from two starts (lavaan’s default and its "simple" start; for OpenMx medfit’s default start and the same start with the tested paths at 0) and compares it with medfit’s mbco_sem() statistic, the best accepted refit of the two linear nulls. It warns only on observed evidence: medfit_warning_engine_constraint_dropped when the engine’s returned fit violates the product constraint (OpenMx at a zero start can drop it), and medfit_warning_engine_statistic_above_max when a feasible run’s statistic exceeds medfit’s (lavaan can stop at the wrong branch). Both inherit from medfit_warning_engine_comparison; a case it cannot judge is "unresolved", never an accusation. Observed-variable covariance models only. The compare-lr gate in tests/sim checks the labeling live on both engines.

Bug fixes

  • The native acceptance gate no longer rejects a correct fit at an active bound because of roundoff (#238). The multiplier slope of a bound is now compared with a floor that scales with the natural-unit gradient norm (1e-10 of it, never below 1e-12), not with the fixed 1e-12. On the reference BLAS (the GitHub Linux runner) the extreme-scale floor fixture of the #213 gate (variances from 1e-3 to 1e3) returned a slope of 2e-12 against a gradient of norm 1e4, was rejected, and left a wrong-branch optimum as the only accepted start; the gate now passes 144 of 144 runs on that BLAS, and the CI gates workflow runs it strict.

medfit 0.11.1

New features

  • Native SEMFit diagnostics now record the best-of-starts verdict in @diagnostics$optimum; summary() prints a concise note when starts disagree or only one start is accepted. Existing optimization warnings are unchanged.

  • anova() on SEMFit records whether each chi-square p-value is valid in the logical attribute p_valid (named by row, NA for the first row). It is FALSE where the null sits on the boundary of the parameter space, the case that already warned. The p-value and the warning are unchanged; code that had to read the warning text can now test attr(x, "p_valid").

Bug fixes

  • anova() on SEMFit refuses a pair where a nonzero fixed parameter (for example M1 ~~ 0.5*M2) is in one fit and absent from the other. Parameter-table inclusion alone let such a pair through, with a chi-square p-value for two models that are not nested. A parameter fixed at a value in one fit and free in the other is still a valid restriction.

  • bootstrap_mediation(method = "nonparametric"), with or without cluster =, now draws every resample in the calling process before the refits are spread over cores. A fixed seed gives the same resamples and boot_estimates for any ncores and for sequential runs; before, each worker drew from its own random-number stream, so ncores changed the result (#247). For a statistic_fn that uses no random numbers, sequential runs keep the stream of 0.11.0, so their results do not change; one that does use them sees a different stream, because its draws no longer interleave with the resampling. ?bootstrap_mediation states what the seed does and does not cover (a statistic_fn that draws random numbers itself, and BLAS thread effects in the last digits).

medfit 0.11.0

New features

  • Factor, character and logical covariates in the native engine. A column of that kind named on a regression’s right side of fit_sem() or fit_mediation(engine = "native") is expanded to 0/1 dummies named <column>_<level> (reference: the first level; character columns sort in the C locale), built before rows with missing values are dropped. g:m expands to one product per dummy, fixed_x = "g" fixes every dummy, mbco_sem() refits through a stored factor map, and four-way extraction accepts a factor covariate in the mediator equation. A label or fixed value on the factor (b*g) stops, as do ordered factors, a product of two factors, and a factor treatment or mediator; the numeric-only error now says where factors are accepted. Numeric-only models are unchanged.
  • A worked example article, “Worked example: study hours, engagement and GPA” (vignettes/articles/example-gpa.qmd): a simulated mediation analysis with known truth, with the delta-method and Sobel formulas written out and a table of 26 pass/fail checks (against the truth, lm, lavaan, the native engine, a bootstrap and a Monte Carlo coverage study). The page stops its own build if a check fails, and tests/testthat/test-example-gpa.R runs the same code.
  • Four-way standard errors can be population-average: options(medfit.covariate_mean_variance = TRUE) adds the sampling variance of the estimated covariate mean, (theta3 * gamma)^2 * Var(c) / n (case-weighted when the fit has weights), to INTref, the NDE and the TE in tidy() and confint(). The default is unchanged (conditional on the observed covariates, as lavaan’s := and the glm route). On simulated data with a strong covariate effect on the mediator, the conditional SE of INTref, 0.0995, becomes 0.1516 against a bootstrap SD of 0.1568; on mediation_demo the term is about 0.08% of the SE.

Bug fixes

  • fit_sem() no longer fails when a supplied start sits in a bad basin. The retries are perturbations of that start, so every attempt could stall; with n_starts >= 3 the last attempt is now the model’s own moment-based start. Found by the reliability gate (latent structure, n = 50, one replicate: 4 of 9600 shipped-configuration fits ended with no start converged; now 0). A start that was accepted before is unchanged, and models with nonlinear constraints keep their starts.

  • medfit installs and loads with development S7 (versions after 0.2.2). The nullable property types (S7::class_numeric | NULL and the list, data frame and call equivalents) and plain S7::class_numeric are registered as S4 unions before the classes use them, in .onLoad() as well as at build time, and the package calls S7’s S7_on_load(), S7_on_unload() and S7_on_build() hooks when the installed S7 has them (S7 0.2.2 and earlier still use methods_register()). Reported and first fixed by t-kalinowski (PR #214); the plain-numeric union was added because the installed package failed to load under development S7 although load_all() worked. No change for users of S7 0.2.2.

  • Nonlinear equality and inequality constraints in the native engine no longer land on a wrong point (#213). A fit such as a*b/sqrt(2*(b^2*Vm+Vy)) == q used to step to a negative variance (no start converged), or stop on the wrong sign branch of the constraint and report converged with a likelihood-ratio statistic of 1459 where 0 is right. Behavior change, for fits with a nonlinear row only (every other fit is bit-identical): the variances that appear in a nonlinear row get a lower bound of 1e-4 times their natural unit (the variable’s variance, so it does not depend on the data scale), and the fit warns when a bound is active; the model without the nonlinear rows is fitted first, and its estimate and sign-flipped copies of it are extra starts; a feasible reference estimate is never replaced by a worse accepted fit, and a fit that reaches it no longer warns that the starts disagree. Checked against an independent profile-likelihood oracle on 24 fixtures at 6 constraint values (tests/sim/sem-nonlinear-profile-gate.R). A residual variance below 1e-4 of the variable’s variance (an R-squared above 0.9999) is outside what a nonlinear row can fit and is reported by the floor warning.

  • AIC() and BIC() with several SEMFit fits now stop when the fits do not share their observed variables, and name the variables that differ. A product term (x:m) adds a column to the joint likelihood, so a fit with a product and the same model without it describe different data; before, the two were ranked anyway (on mediation_demo, the same outcome gave AIC 3934.7 with the product and 2994.1 without). anova() and mbco_sem() already refused such a pair (#206).

  • A fit with nonlinear constraints that found exactly one optimum among its starts (every other start failed or was rejected) was returned without a note, although the failed starts are often the sign-flipped ones that would have found another branch. It now warns “only 1 of N starts reached an accepted solution”. Found by running the simulation gates on a Linux runner with the reference BLAS, where the #213 floor fixture at an extreme data scale (R-squared of 1 - 1e-6) kept a wrong-branch optimum silently; that fixture’s underlying instability at the floor is tracked separately.

Lifecycle

  • The native maximum-likelihood engine (fit_sem(), mbco_sem(), SEMFit, fit_mediation(engine = "native")) is no longer marked experimental. It met the written exit criteria in planning/specs/CRITERIA-native-experimental-exit-2026-10-17.csv: all 17 native simulation gates re-run green on this code (tests/sim/run-gates.R), lavaan and OpenMx parity hold, and no correctness issue is open. From now on the exported signatures, the SEMFit properties and the model-syntax grammar in ?medfit-syntax change only through a deprecation; numerical fixes are not breaking changes. New syntax and new properties are added without changing what an existing name means: the planned categorical mediators, outcomes and treatments will arrive as additions (the dummy names such as g_b and the product name m:x stay), and tests/testthat/test-api-freeze.R pins the current names, argument order and grammar so a rename fails the suite.

Documentation

  • Removed a literal header file path and a literal Version {version} footer placeholder that the website printed; mathematics uses the built-in MathJax support in pkgdown. README installation guidance now distinguishes available binaries from source installation.

medfit 0.10.0

New features

  • The native engine reads a product term, :, in a regression: y ~ x + m + x:m (fit_sem() and fit_mediation(engine = "native", model = )). The product is an observed exogenous variable whose column x * m the engine builds from data after listwise deletion, as lavaan does, so the likelihood, the constraints and the mean structure are unchanged. x:m and m:x are one term; the table, tidy() and the extraction use the canonical name, the two factor names sorted in the C locale (m:x for x and m), and a label (b*x:m) names the coefficient. Writing both spellings in one equation is an error that names both. A product term always turns the mean structure on (meanstructure = FALSE with a product is an error), because the four-way decomposition needs the mediator intercept. A column already in data under either spelling is used only if it equals x * m on the rows kept, and otherwise stops with a message that names the column; with fixed_x = TRUE the product column is fixed at its sample moments with the other exogenous variables.

  • extract_mediation() on a SEMFit now returns the four-way decomposition (InteractionMediationData) when the outcome equation carries the treatment-by-mediator product; decomposition = "four_way" and interaction = (the product written with :) work, and without the product decomposition = "four_way" is refused with a message that says to add x:m. This replaces the 0.9.0 refusal. On a simple model the four-way parts equal the glm route to the printed digits, and on mediation_demo the native and lavaan coefficients and sandwich standard errors agree to the printed digits. The estimate names and outcome_predictors carry the canonical m:x; the lavaan route keeps the spelling you wrote. Any other product involving the treatment or the mediator is refused on this route. Centering matters: the reference level m_star = 0 and E[M | X = 0] depend on where the mediator is centered, so CDE and INTref move with centering while NDE, NIE and the total do not (the native four-way article shows this).

Supported class for a product (limits)

A model with a product is fitted only inside the class below; anything else is an error that names the feature and says it is not yet supported with products. A model without a product keeps every 0.9.0 capability.

  • Recursive models; no residual covariance between observed outcomes (a ~~ between outcomes, or a free one; the covariance that completion would add between pure outcomes is fixed at 0 with one note, and the same model without the product estimates it); no shared label, fixed coefficient, bound, or ==, <, > constraint on a coefficient; intercepts free, not shared and unconstrained; no outcome-derived regressor (a product factor that is the target or one of its descendants). := parameters are allowed. Exogenous products and products of two exogenous variables (x:w) are inside the class; latent products, x:x and three-way products are not supported.

  • Model tests. When a product factor is itself a regression target, or the exogenous (co)variance block is restricted, the global chi-square is not valid, so glance() reports chi-square, df and p-value as NA with a note, summary() and print() show the note, anova() and mbco_sem() refuse naming the product, and information = "expected" is refused for a product with an endogenous factor (use the default observed information with se_type = "sandwich"). logLik(), AIC and BIC stay defined. fit_sem() warns once when the model test is unavailable and once when a product is fitted without se_type = "sandwich". A product of exogenous variables with a free exogenous block keeps the ordinary test (null simulation, 1000 replications, n = 500: rejection 0.055 and 0.056 at nominal 0.05 for normal and centered-exponential factors).

  • The product depends on the 0.9.0 mean structure (a product turns it on) and on fixed_x (a fixed set includes the product columns). The native four-way read uses the shared worker, so it carries the corrections shipped in 0.9.0 (standard errors that include the mediator-covariate term, an error for a treatment product in the mediator equation, weighted covariate means in INTref; see “Behavior changes” under 0.9.0 below).

medfit 0.9.0

New features

  • The native engine fits observed intercepts and means. Any y ~ 1 row (or meanstructure = TRUE in fit_sem() and engine_args = list(meanstructure = TRUE) in fit_mediation()) turns the mean structure on and frees every observed intercept the model does not write, as lavaan does. The fit works in mean-centered coordinates, so data far from zero (checked to a mean of 1e5 standard deviations) no longer ruins the information matrix; intercepts can be constrained or bounded (checked to a mean of 1e3 standard deviations). Weights, the sandwich covariance, linear and nonlinear constraints, anova() (a covariance-only fit counts as having free intercepts), mbco_sem() and fit_mediation(engine = "native") all work with it. The four-way decomposition on a native fit is refused by name until the : operator arrives (planned for 0.10.0).

  • fit_sem(fixed_x = ) (and fit_mediation(engine = "native", engine_args = list(fixed_x = ))) fixes the mean, variance and covariances of exogenous observed variables at their sample values, as lavaan’s fixed.x = TRUE does. TRUE selects every exogenous observed variable (product columns included) and a character vector selects any subset; the default stays FALSE. The structural estimates, their standard errors (model-based and sandwich), the degrees of freedom and the chi-square do not change; the parameter count falls, and the fixed rows stay in @table, tidy() and summary() with a fixed_x flag and no standard error. On one simulated model with 30 covariates (n = 400, Apple M5 Pro) the fit went from 561 to 65 parameters and from about 5 seconds to about 0.2 seconds; your timing will differ.

Behavior changes

  • With fixed_x, logLik(), AIC() and BIC() are conditional on the fixed variables (lavaan’s value), so anova(), mbco_sem() and multi-fit AIC()/BIC() now stop when the fits’ fixed sets or data differ. A (co)variance or intercept statement on a selected variable is an error; lavaan keeps such a statement free and lets the degrees of freedom move. glance() for a SEMFit gains a fixed_x column ("" when nothing is fixed), and print() and summary() say what the log likelihood is conditional on. fixed_x = FALSE results are unchanged.

  • A fixed intercept, y ~ 0*1, is now a restriction in the native engine. 0.8.0 dropped the row and returned the covariance-only fit; 0.9.0 reads it as “the mean of y is 0”, which costs one degree of freedom, changes the discrepancy, and can be compared with anova() against the fit that frees it. Any y ~ 1 row (free, fixed or labeled) now turns the mean structure on and frees every unwritten observed intercept, as lavaan does; meanstructure = FALSE with an intercept is an error. A model without ~1 rows is unchanged.

  • Names without dots. Everything medfit names now uses snake_case: tidy() and glance() columns std.error, p.value, conf.low and conf.high became std_error, p_value, conf_low and conf_high, and the tidy() arguments conf.int and conf.level became conf_int and conf_level; the old argument names still work and warn. The S3 classes of summary() results are now summary_MediationData, summary_SEMFit and so on. mbco_sem() keeps p.value, because it returns a base-R htest. Update code that reads the old column names.

  • anova() and mbco_sem() for SEMFit close two more gaps in their guards. The nesting check now also keeps the equalities that repeated labels impose in the larger model (M ~ a*X, Y ~ a*M): releasing the shared label no longer returns a chi-square p-value. The boundary warning now covers an active nonlinear inequality (a*b > 0 at the restricted fit), which it missed before.

  • anova() for SEMFit no longer reports a p-value for a restricted model that is not nested in the larger one through constraints. The nesting check compared only the free parameters, so a == b against a == 0 and b == 0.5 (the second breaks the first) returned a chi-square p-value. The restricted model must now keep every fixed value, bound and constraint of the larger one (a bound includes a single-label inequality such as a > 0.1): a linear equality must follow from the restricted model’s equalities and fixed values, and a nonlinear equality or an inequality must appear verbatim. Comparisons that are not nested now stop with “not nested”.

  • Four-way decomposition from a lavaan fit (extract_mediation() with an x:m or interaction = product) gave wrong results in three cases, now fixed:

    • The standard errors of INTref, NDE and TE left out the mediator-covariate term (g * cbar and its covariance with the mediator intercept), so they were too small when the mediator equation has a covariate (INTref SE 0.037 against lavaan’s := 0.095 in one check). They now match lavaan’s :=.
    • A treatment product in the mediator equation (m ~ x + w + x:w), or a treatment-by-covariate product in the outcome equation, returned a wrong decomposition without a message. Both are now errors that name the equation.
    • With sampling weights, INTref used unweighted covariate means, so it differed from the lm/glm route (1.16 against 1.46 on one data set). It now uses the weighted means.
    • Related: a mediator predictor that is not a numeric column of the model data (for example a latent variable) is now an error (“Cannot compute the covariate means for E[M | X = 0]”); it used to be skipped, which dropped its contribution from INTref without a message. A weighted multi-group fit is an error as well. Point estimates change only for the weighted case and for covariates that used to be skipped. The effects are the treatment contrast 0 to 1, as on the lm/glm route.

Documentation

  • Two new pages for the native engine, in the Guides menu: “Native engine in five minutes” (write, fit, read, test, constrain, extract) and “The native engine guide” (syntax, fitting and reading, standard errors and weights, constraints and how each kind is solved, model comparison and the MBCO test, diagnostics, the route to the mediation objects, limits). A third page, “Native engine, step by step”, walks the same path in nine checked steps, including a chain of three paths and, in the last step, fixed_x.

  • The constraints page and the introduction no longer say native constraints must be linear: nonlinear constraints, anova() for nested fits and mbco_sem(paths = ) are described there.

  • Cookbook recipes 14 to 17: compare two native models with anova(), a defined parameter with its interval, a bound or a fixed path with the diagnostics, and checking a native fit before trusting it. Recipe 18 fixes the exogenous covariates with fixed_x. The cookbook now has eighteen recipes.

medfit 0.8.0

New features

  • anova() for SEMFit: the likelihood-ratio test for nested fits, anova(fit_full, fit_restricted) or several fits in a chain. It reports each fit’s chi-square (n times the discrepancy), the difference, its degrees of freedom and the p-value, and reproduces the per-refit statistics of mbco_sem() (221.05 and 0.083 on RMediation’s memory_exp). It compares fits that were already made and never refits. Fits on different data or variables, with sampling weights, that did not converge, with equal degrees of freedom, or where the restricted fit frees a parameter the other leaves out are refused, and a null on the boundary of the parameter space (an active bound or inequality on a tested parameter) warns that the p-value is not valid, as mbco_sem() does. Nesting is checked by parameter-table inclusion, which is necessary and not sufficient.

  • tidy(), glance() and confint() for SEMFit. tidy() returns one row per free and defined parameter (term, op, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, and the interval with conf.int = TRUE); glance() returns one row with nobs, npar, df, the chi-square test against the saturated model, logLik, AIC and BIC; confint() covers the defined parameters too. All agree with lavaan on a shared model to about 1e-9. glance() has no converged column: fit_sem() returns a fit only for an accepted solution, so @converged is TRUE for every SEMFit and carries no information (now documented). A fit with sampling weights has no likelihood, so its chi-square, logLik, AIC and BIC are NA.

  • Nonlinear equality constraints in fit_sem() and fit_mediation(engine = "native"): cp == a*b, a*b == 0.1, exp(a) == 1 and any equality built from the allowed functions are solved by SLSQP with the constraint’s value and Jacobian recomputed at every point (the Jacobian by central differences). The covariance is projected onto the null space of the Jacobian at the solution, and the degrees of freedom count the equalities’ rank there. The fit matches OpenMx’s constrained optimum to 1e-5 and the standard errors agree with a reparameterized fit and a bootstrap. Nonlinear inequalities are covered in the next entry. A product of labels set to zero (a*b == 0, b1*b2*b3 == 0, also through a := name) is not solved by the nonlinear route, whose Jacobian vanishes at the solution: it is a == 0 or b == 0, so the model is refitted once per factor from the default start and the smallest discrepancy wins (fit@internals$branch names the winning line). On RMediation’s memory_exp the a1*b1 == 0 statistic is the exact 0.083100, where a nonlinear solve lands on 221.05. Several zero-product lines give the cartesian product of branches (at most 64).

  • mbco_sem() tests a product of k labeled paths: mbco_sem(fit, paths = c("a", "d", "b")) (or a vector in a with b missing) refits once per path, keeps the smallest diffLL and refers it to chi-square(1). With two paths it gives exactly the old result (mbco_sem(fit, "a", "b") still works). The null is a union of k hypotheses, so the test is conservative. A simulation gate (tests/sim/sem-mbco-k-size.R, 2000 replications per cell) found the size at most 0.055 at alpha = 0.05 with one zero path and under 0.005 with two or three.

  • Nonlinear inequality constraints in fit_sem(): a*b > 0.1, a*b < 0.5, and a defined name inside a constraint (ab := a*b then ab > 0) are solved like the nonlinear equalities, as rows c(theta) <= 0 with a recomputed Jacobian. The acceptance test for a curved constraint now uses the reduced Hessian of the Lagrangian, the objective’s Hessian plus each active nonlinear row’s curvature times its multiplier; the objective’s Hessian alone can call a saddle of the restricted problem a minimum (or the reverse). n_starts changes meaning for a model with a nonlinear constraint: every start is tried and the best accepted one is kept (before, the first accepted start was used), and a warning says when the accepted starts reached different optima, because a nonlinear constraint can leave several (a*b > 0.1 is feasible for two positive or two negative paths). Models without a nonlinear constraint behave as before.

  • A sum of products set to zero (a1*b1 + a2*b2 == 0) fits through the same nonlinear route and is documented as best-effort: unlike a single product it has no exact reduction, so the result is the best of the starts tried, and the starts-disagree warning means a better optimum may exist (raise n_starts).

Behavior changes

  • A SEMFit has one spelling for a parameter: its label, else lhs op rhs without spaces, as lavaan names coefficients. coef(), vcov(), tidy() and the accessors extract_mediation() reads now agree. Before, coef() of an unlabeled parameter read "M ~ X" and "X ~~ X" (with spaces) while the accessors read "M~X", and a latent loading was named like a regression into its indicator ("m2 ~ eta", with tidy() reporting op as =~). Now the names are "M~X", "X~~X" and "eta=~m2", and they equal names(lavaan::coef()) on a shared model. Code that indexed coef(fit) by an unlabeled spaced name must drop the spaces; labeled parameters are unchanged. The wrong names were never part of a release’s documented interface (SEMFit is experimental).

  • fit_sem(weights = ) replaces fit_sem(sampling_weights = ), the name fit_mediation() already uses, and mbco_sem(object, a, b) replaces mbco_sem(fit, a, b), the name the other SEMFit methods use. The old names still work and warn once per session with lifecycle; positional calls are unaffected.

Bug fixes

  • Native SEM fits with an active nonlinear constraint (cp == a*b, a*b > k, a*b + cp == 0) are polished after the solver is accepted. SLSQP stops along a flat constraint tangent, so estimates could sit up to 4e-5 from the exact optimum; a few Newton steps on the KKT system (using the Lagrangian Hessian) now bring them within 1e-10 of a fit with the constraint solved out. The acceptance gate is unchanged and is re-run on the polished point, which replaces the accepted one only if it is accepted again.

  • fit_sem() now gives the same verdict on a wrong-side active bound whether or not the model has constraint lines. A solution sitting at a bound with the gradient pointing into the interior (a point that is not a local minimum) was rejected for a model without constraints but accepted with a warning once any ==, < or > line was added, even one that never binds. It is now rejected in both cases, and the next start is tried; each bound is judged by the same statistic, the gradient over the root of the Hessian diagonal, so an indefinite Hessian cannot hide it. A wrong-signed active inequality constraint still warns and does not reject. Behavior change: a fit that returned with the warning “lower bound of … is active, but moving into the feasible region would lower the objective” now errors or uses another start. fit_sem() is experimental and no dependent package uses it, so there is no deprecation period.

  • nobs(), @n_obs and med() no longer overstate the sample size when the data have missing values on the model variables. The lm/glm extractors counted nrow(data) although glm() had dropped the incomplete rows, so a fit with 5 missing treatment values reported 400 observations on 395 rows. n_obs now counts the rows the models used, and the stored @data drops the same rows, so the four-way covariate means use them too. fit_mediation() drops rows that are incomplete on any variable in either formula before fitting, so the mediator and outcome models share one sample; extract_mediation() warns when models you fitted yourself used different rows. The estimates are unchanged when the models already used the same rows; the native and lmer engines already counted correctly.

  • fit_mediation() applies subset, weights, offset, etastart and mustart to the rows you passed, then drops incomplete rows. After #138 a subset containing an incomplete row selected the next row instead, and a vector offset stopped the fit with a length error. n_obs now counts the rows the models used when subset is given.

  • fit_mediation(engine = "lmer") now stops with an error when either formula contains an offset(). The engine rebuilds both formulas from their terms, which exclude offsets, so the offset was dropped without a word and the fit was the same as without it.

  • Joint mediation effects (several mediators with treatment-by-mediator products) now check that every variable two models share holds the same values in the same order, not only that the row names agree. A mediator model fitted to a reordered copy of the data with its row names reset used to pass, and the cross-equation covariance, and with it the joint effect intervals, was silently wrong.

  • Fits made with na.action = na.exclude no longer break the extraction. The joint covariance came back with NA blocks and NA effect intervals and no error, and the residual standard deviation of a Gaussian glm() stopped extract_mediation() with a missing-value error.

  • fit_sem() now rejects a self-regression (Y ~ Y) and a repeated row (Y ~ X twice, or X ~~ Y and Y ~~ X) at parse time, naming the row. Before, Y ~ Y failed late with “no start converged” and a repeated row with “a path appears twice in the RAM specification”. Infeasible bounds (a > 1 with a < 0.5) now stop with a message naming the parameter and both bounds instead of an internal assertion.

  • fit_sem() now accepts a consistent set whose inequality repeats an equality: a == b with a - b < 0, or a + b == 0.8 with a + b > 0.8. These sets stopped with “no start converged” on 5 to 7 of 12 simulated datasets, because the inequality is active at every feasible point and gave the optimizer a rank-deficient active Jacobian. The optimizer now gets the rows without an inequality that the equality rows imply and satisfy; the acceptance gate still checks every row, so an implied inequality the equalities violate (a + b == 0.8 with a + b < 0.5) is still reported as violated. Behavior change: sets that errored now fit, and the estimates equal those of the model with the redundant inequality deleted.

Documentation

  • Cookbook recipe 12 shows a nonlinear constraint (cp == a*b) and the indirect effect of a three-path chain with mbco_sem(paths = ). The 0.7.0 entry for fit_mediation(engine = "native") no longer says it handles serial and parallel mediators; it takes one mediator, and model-native-multi already said so.

  • New article “lavaan and the native engine” (Guides menu): both engines run on mediation_demo at site build, then a feature table lists what each does with a status for every row. test-lavaan-comparison.R computes each status from a live probe against lavaan, so a row cannot change without the behavior changing.

  • Every cookbook recipe from 1 to 8 now runs after the setup chunk alone. Recipes 3, 6, 7 and 8 used fitted models that only an earlier recipe created, which running the page top to bottom hid; a test now runs each recipe in a fresh environment.

  • The cookbook and Getting Started no longer present survey weights as covered by se_type = "sandwich": HC3 standard errors treat the observations as independent, so they do not handle survey clusters, strata or replicate weights.

  • The home page now leads with the r-universe and GitHub installs of 0.7.0 and says that CRAN 0.3.2 does not run the examples (it lacks mediation_demo, fit_sem(), mbco_sem() and the joint and cluster classes). Getting Started, the cookbook and the Reference Card state the version they need.

  • Getting Started and the Introduction now cover the cluster and native engines (an engine table, the two classes, and a fit_sem() example), and the Model Extraction article has a section on extracting from a SEMFit. ?extract_mediation lists the SEMFit method and the ClusterMediationData return, and no longer names brms as a supported model type; it is still future work.

  • ?SEMFit, ?SEMFit-methods and ?"medfit-syntax" now have examples that run.

  • The Model Extraction article has a “Which section do I need?” table at the top, ends on Next Steps, and sets three dense paragraphs as bullets. The Methods article’s cluster and native engine sections now have subheadings.

  • The Introduction counted SEMFit as the seventh class; it is the eighth. Its Package Ecosystem list now names probmed and medrobust, and the Reference Card gives joint_effects() its real argument names (object, estimates).

  • New Models menu and landing page, and a Cookbook menu in the top menu bar. The Models page has a capability matrix and a “find your model” table; eight model pages cover simple mediation, binary and non-normal variables, treatment-by-mediator interaction, weights and robust standard errors, the regmedint engine, serial, parallel and joint mediation. Articles are now grouped in an index. A test keeps every model page on the landing page, in the index and in the menu, and every cookbook anchor real.

  • Six more model pages: cluster-randomized trials (2-1-1), lavaan fits, and four on the native engine (paths and defined parameters, a latent mediator, constraints and the MBCO test, several mediators and weights). They join the Models menu, the landing page and the articles index. A test triggers each error message the pages quote, so a reworded message fails the tests before a page goes stale.

  • A new “Guides” menu and group with four pages: What changed since CRAN 0.3.2 (the results that changed and the calls that now stop with an error), Troubleshooting (the errors and warnings a user is most likely to hit, each with its cause and fix), Which interval should I use?, and a Glossary of terms and symbols. Tests trigger every message the guides quote and check the known answers behind their claims.

  • The home page and Getting Started are rewritten so they are quick to skim: a “What’s new” table, a 60-second start, a “pick your model” table, long examples folded away, and Getting Started cut to four steps that link to the model pages. A test checks that their article links and cookbook anchors are real.

  • The Models page states that fit_mediation(engine = "native") takes one mediator; for several, fit with fit_sem() and call extract_mediation().

  • The bootstrap example in the README printed NIE = 0.19 [0.08, 0.32] | NDE = 0.16 | PM = 55%, which no longer matched the code or its own non-bootstrap fit on the same data; it now shows NIE = 0.164 [0.0867, 0.256] | NDE = 0.293 | PM = 36 %. Its feature list, function list and test count now include the lmer engine, cluster decomposition and native fits.

medfit 0.7.0

medfit 0.7.0 adds an experimental native maximum-likelihood structural equation engine. It is released on GitHub and r-universe only and is not submitted to CRAN.

New features

  • New native maximum-likelihood structural equation engine (experimental). fit_sem(model, data) fits lavaan-style model syntax to raw data and returns a SEMFit with print(), summary(), coef(), vcov(), nobs() and logLik(). It handles observed and latent variables, labels, fixed values, starts and bounds, linear equality and inequality constraints (==, <, >), and defined parameters (:=) with delta-method standard errors. The syntax is documented in ?"medfit-syntax", including the two medfit extensions (comma shorthand and CONSTRAINT(...)).
  • fit_mediation(engine = "native", model = , treatment = , mediator = ) fits the syntax and returns the usual mediation objects, for an observed or a latent single mediator (which need not be a column of data); serial and parallel mediators go through fit_sem() and then extract_mediation(fit, mediator = c(...), outcome = ), because fit_mediation() takes one mediator. extract_mediation() has a method for SEMFit that shares its workers with the lavaan route, so the aliases and covariance rows are the same; its source_package is "medfit". For an observed single mediator, probmed::pmed() runs on the native route with the plugin estimator and the parametric bootstrap, which agrees with the glm route within Monte Carlo error; a latent mediator supports the plugin estimator only (#105).
  • Standard errors use observed information by default (information = "expected" is available). Against OpenMx they agree to 1.6e-4 in the worst of 240 simulated datasets; expected information for latent-variable models differs from that reference by up to 11% at n = 50, which is why observed is the default. Under equality constraints and at active bounds the covariance is projected onto the feasible directions, so a constrained parameter has zero variance and a == b gives the standard error of the collapsed model.
  • Sampling weights and robust standard errors: fit_sem(sampling_weights = , se_type = "sandwich") fits weighted maximum likelihood on the weighted mean and covariance with the sandwich covariance from casewise scores, and fit_mediation(engine = "native", weights = , se_type = "sandwich") takes the same two arguments the glm engine does. The native sandwich is HC0-type: it equals sandwich::vcovHC(type = "HC0") per equation and lavaan’s robust standard errors with sampling.weights (to 1e-6 and 1e-5), so it is a few percent narrower than the glm engine’s HC3 default at moderate n, a gap that shrinks like 1/n. logLik() is not defined for a weighted fit.
  • mbco_sem(fit, a, b) tests the indirect effect in a fit_sem() fit as the minimum of two likelihood-ratio tests: it refits with a == 0 and with b == 0 (two linear solves), takes the smaller diffLL as the statistic, and refers it to chi-square with one degree of freedom. The result is an htest that also carries both diffLL values. It reproduces OpenMx’s diffLL on RMediation’s memory_exp to 1e-6 (221.045546 and 0.083100) and lavaan’s constrained fits on a latent-mediator model. It tests a product of two labeled regression paths, refuses a fit with sampling weights or one that did not converge, has its refits inherit the fit’s n_starts and control, and warns when a bound or an inequality on the tested path puts the null on the boundary of the parameter space. The nonlinear a*b == 0 is deliberately not solved: a nonlinear solver can stop at the branch with the larger statistic.
  • Not yet supported by the native engine: mean structures (free intercepts), the four-way decomposition (it needs the mediator intercept; use decomposition = "two_way"), standardized estimates, and multilevel models. Nonlinear constraints are planned for a later release; until then a nonlinear constraint is an error that names the constraint.

Bug fixes

  • bootstrap_mediation(cluster = ) no longer discards every replicate when the statistic refits through fit_mediation(engine = "lmer") with fewer than 25 clusters. The few-cluster warning (fewer than 25 clusters with model-based standard errors, or fewer than 10 with any standard error) was counted as a failed refit, so the bootstrap that the warning recommends stopped with “Too many bootstrap samples failed”. The warning now has the condition class medfit_few_clusters and is not counted; the point estimate on the original data still shows it once. In 0.6.0, se_type = "kr" with 10 or more clusters avoids the warning and so avoids the failure.

Behavior change

  • fit_mediation() has a new named argument model. An argument passed to stats::glm() through ... that partially matches it, such as mod = FALSE, now binds to model instead, and model is an error with the glm engine. Spelling out model = FALSE does not help: drop the argument. glm()’s own model argument cannot be passed through fit_mediation().

  • extract_mediation() on a lavaan fit of a simple single-mediator model now appends the rows m_<treatment>, y_<mediator> and y_<treatment> to @estimates and @vcov of the returned MediationData. These are the names the lm/glm route already used, so code that resolves coefficients by name, such as probmed::pmed(method = "parametric_bootstrap"), now works on lavaan-derived objects instead of failing with a subscript-out-of-bounds error. Each new row repeats the a, b or c_prime path with the same estimate and covariances; every existing row keeps its name, value and position. Code that indexes @estimates or @vcov by position past the a, b, c_prime rows, or that counts their rows, sees three more. A lavaan fit with a latent or ordered treatment, mediator or outcome, and any standardized = TRUE extraction, gets none of the three rows and supports the plugin estimators only. Serial, parallel and four-way objects are unchanged (#106).

Documentation

  • The cookbook has an eleventh recipe, a latent mediator fitted with the native engine and tested with mbco_sem(). The model syntax is documented in ?"medfit-syntax", the Methods and Formulas article has a section on the native engine with a subsection on MBCO, and the Reference Card lists fit_sem(), mbco_sem() and the SEMFit class.

Dependencies

  • lifecycle is now in Imports, and the lifecycle badge figures ship in man/figures/. Deprecations and experimental features are marked with it.
  • nloptr (>= 1.0.4) is now in Imports: the native engine uses its SLSQP solver. It contains compiled code, so a source install from GitHub (for example pak::pak("data-wise/medfit")) builds it unless lme4 already brought it in; the r-universe binaries need no compiler.
  • OpenMx is now in Suggests. Only the tests use it, as the independent reference for standard errors and for mbco_sem().

medfit 0.6.0

New features

  • New ClusterMediationData class and an lmer method for extract_mediation(): mediation for a treatment assigned to whole clusters (such as schools), with the mediator and outcome measured on individuals (the 2-1-1 design). Pass the mediator model M ~ X + ... + (1 | cluster) as object and the outcome model as model_y, both fitted with lme4::lmer() on the same rows. The outcome model must carry the mediator as its within-cluster deviation plus the observed cluster mean, or the raw mediator plus the cluster mean (the within parameterization is recovered from it); medfit finds these terms by value, so grand-mean centering and scale() work. The natural indirect effect is a * b_between; decompose() splits it into an own-mediator part a * b_within and a spillover part a * (b_between - b_within), labeled as the cluster-average, large-cluster approximation, with a warning when the approximation error exceeds half the own effect’s standard error. print() and summary() end with an “Estimand and assumptions” block. nie(), nde(), te(), pm(), paths(), decompose(), coef(), vcov(), nobs(), confint(), tidy(), glance() and quick() support the class, and the parametric bootstrap accepts it. Standard errors are delta-method SEs from lme4’s model-based covariance. Treatment-by-mediator and covariate-by-mediator products, non-Gaussian (glmer) fits and random slopes on anything but the within term are errors. lme4 is in Suggests.

  • fit_mediation(engine = "lmer", cluster = ) fits the two linear mixed models of the cluster design (REML, random cluster intercepts, the mediator and any level-1 covariates split into a within-cluster deviation and a cluster mean) and returns a ClusterMediationData. se_type = "kr" applies the Kenward-Roger adjustment (pbkrtest, in Suggests; REML fits only): each path gets a Kenward-Roger denominator degrees of freedom in @kr_df, and confint() and tidy(conf.int = TRUE) give t intervals for the paths while the product effects keep normal intervals. extract_mediation() warns per call when there are fewer than 25 clusters with model-based standard errors, and when there are fewer than 10 clusters with any standard error type. The methods article has a new 2-1-1 section: models, effects, the own/spillover approximation and its exact form, the covariance argument and the assumptions table.

  • Fix: the ?ClusterMediationData reference now cites Talloen et al. (2016, Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics) correctly; the entry in the development version cited a different title and journal.

  • bootstrap_mediation() gains cluster = for method = "nonparametric": it resamples whole clusters with replacement and gives each draw a fresh cluster id before statistic_fn sees the data, so a cluster drawn twice is refit as two clusters rather than one larger one. Singular fits and convergence warnings from a refit count as failures: they are excluded, their messages are suppressed, and their number is added to the existing warning. cluster = NULL (the default) resamples rows as before; cluster with the parametric or plugin methods is an error.

  • extract_mediation() on two lmer fits now stops when the fits kept different individuals within the same clusters (the same number of rows, the same cluster vector and the same treatment values, but different rows). It used to fall through to a misleading “no cluster-mean term” error, and could pair rows incorrectly if values coincided. The check compares the data row names the fits kept, so it cannot see a mismatch between frames whose row names were both reset (a tibble, for example). ?extract_mediation no longer lists lmerMod as future.

  • The 30 internal helper functions (names starting with a dot) no longer have Rd pages, so the package site stops publishing 30 unlisted dot-* reference pages. No user-facing function changes.

  • fit_mediation(engine = "lmer") now stops with a clear error when a formula contains a random-effect term such as (1 | id): the engine adds the random cluster intercept itself, and the term used to reach lmer() as a fixed term and fail with Invalid grouping factor specification. The message names the formula and points to engine_args for random slopes. I(a | b) as a covariate is not affected.

Documentation

  • New “Reference Card” article listing every export and class on one page, and a “Cookbook” article with ten task recipes (a first fit through cluster designs). Both are linked from the site menu and README; tests check that the card names every export and that each recipe’s code and links resolve. The cluster examples on ?fit_mediation, ?bootstrap_mediation and ?extract_mediation now run, and Getting Started and Introduction point to the new pages.

medfit 0.5.0

Two fixes change results (marked Behavior change below): serial te() and pm() now sum every path (#81), and confint(parm = "paths") finds path rows by name instead of by position (#82). Both correct wrong output, so they ship without a deprecation period. Ecosystem: probmed and RMediation call neither function and their test suites pass against this release. The same bugs are present in CRAN 0.3.2; see #83 for workarounds.

New features

  • New JointMediationData class: extract_mediation() on lm/glm fits with two or more mediators (serial or parallel) now supports treatment-by-mediator product terms in the outcome model, written with : or * (e.g. Y ~ X * M2 + M1 + C). It returns the joint natural effects of the mediators as a block (VanderWeele and Vansteelandt 2014): for a 0/1 treatment, NIE = sum over mediators of (theta2 + theta3) times the total treatment effect on that mediator, NDE and CDE add the product terms at the covariate means and at m_star. There is no per-mediator split of the NIE. For a serial chain the joint NIE counts every path through the mediators, so it differs from the chain-only a * d * b that nie() reports by default for SerialMediationData (it matches nie(type = "total") when there is no product term). Standard errors use analytic delta-method gradients and a stacked-OLS covariance that includes the correlation between parallel mediator equations; they are conditional on the observed covariates. nie(), nde(), te(), pm(), decompose(), paths(), print(), summary(), coef(), vcov(), nobs(), confint(parm = "paths" / "effects"), tidy() (types "paths" and "effects", with delta-method SEs) and glance() (adding structure, n_mediators, interactions and m_star) support the class. The new joint_effects() recomputes the effects at any parameter vector, which makes it the statistic for a parametric bootstrap_mediation(). The “Model Extraction” article has a worked example on mediation_demo$outcome_int. The fit must use Gaussian identity-link models without weights, an intercept in each, the same rows and the same covariates in every model, a numeric 0/1 treatment, and every mediator in the outcome model; each violation errors, naming the cause. m_star is a scalar or a vector named by the interacting mediators. Products elsewhere (in a mediator model, mediator-by-mediator, three-way, with a covariate, or function-wrapped) still error, as do lavaan multi-mediator fits with products.

  • New bundled dataset mediation_demo (400 rows, 8 variables): simulated data that supports simple, serial, parallel, and treatment-by-mediator interaction examples from one running example. The covariates are mediator-outcome confounders, so examples adjust for them. See ?mediation_demo for the generating equations; the generating script is in data-raw/. The “Getting Started”, “Introduction”, and “Model Extraction” articles and the single-mediator examples for fit_mediation(), extract_mediation(), med(), quick(), bootstrap_mediation(), nie(), nde(), te(), pm(), and paths() now use it, adjusting for both covariates.

  • bootstrap_mediation(method = "parametric") and method = "plugin" now accept SerialMediationData, ParallelMediationData, and InteractionMediationData, not only MediationData. Both methods read only @estimates and @vcov, which every class carries with matching names, so statistic_fn can use the path aliases directly (e.g. a * d1 * b for a serial chain, a1 * b1 + a2 * b2 for parallel mediators). Previously these classes were rejected because they do not inherit from MediationData.

  • BootstrapResult gains coef() and confint() methods. coef() returns c(estimate = ...); confint() returns the stored percentile interval as a 1 x 2 matrix, recomputes it from the bootstrap distribution when a different level is given, and returns NA with a warning for plugin results. Previously both errored with “Can’t get S7 properties with $”.

  • tidy() and glance() now support ParallelMediationData and InteractionMediationData; previously both errored with “not implemented for this S7 object type”. tidy() returns path rows (a1, b1, ..., c_prime or a, b, c_prime, theta3) with standard errors from vcov(), then effect rows (nie, nde, te, plus the four-way cde, int_ref, int_med, pie for interaction models) with delta-method standard errors (see below). glance() adds n_mediators (parallel) or interaction and m_star (interaction).

  • tidy() now reports delta-method standard errors for effect rows (NIE, NDE, TE, and the four-way components) for all four mediation classes, from the same computation as confint(parm = "effects"), so tidy(conf.int = TRUE) reproduces confint() exactly. Previously these rows had NA standard errors, and SerialMediationData returned NA intervals with a warning. tidy() stays silent; ?tidy.S7_object documents that the intervals are normal approximations and that the proportion mediated should be bootstrapped.

  • New confint() method for SerialMediationData, with parm = "paths" or "effects".

Bug fixes

  • extract_mediation() on a lavaan fit with sampling weights no longer fails with “Number of rows in data must match n_obs”. lavaan normalizes the weights to sum to N, so its nobs can read N - 1e-13 (355.99999999999994 for N = 356), and n_obs was truncated to N - 1. It is now rounded. This affects the mediation, parallel, serial and interaction extractors.

  • Behavior change: confint(parm = "paths") now finds each path’s row of @vcov by name: the alias rows (a, b, c_prime; d1, …; a1, b1, …; theta3) first, then, for MediationData, the lm-style m_<treatment>, y_<mediator>, y_<treatment> rows. Names come from rownames(x@vcov), or from names(x@estimates) when x@vcov has none. Previously MediationData looked only for the lm-style names and otherwise warned and took the first three diagonal entries. That gave wrong SEs for every lavaan-extracted object, where rows 1-3 are a, c’, b, so b and c’ swapped SEs. It was right for a hand-built object with alias names only when those came first. The serial, parallel, interaction and joint methods returned NA bounds for a missing row. All five now error, naming the missing rows, when neither set of names resolves. tidy() still reports NA there, as it is descriptive; confint() is strict. Ecosystem note: downstream code that builds these objects by hand with unnamed @estimates/@vcov gets an error from confint(parm = "paths") instead of a warning or NA.

  • Behavior change: te() and pm() for SerialMediationData now use the full total effect, the sum over every X-to-Y path, instead of only the chain plus the direct effect (a * d * b + c'). For the usual specification (M2 ~ X + M1, Y ~ X + M1 + M2) the old value left out the paths that skip a mediator (X -> M1 -> Y, X -> M2 -> Y) and could be badly off. In one simulated example it gave 0.13 where the true total effect was 0.54. With linear models and the same covariates in every equation, te() now equals the treatment coefficient of lm(Y ~ X + covariates). pm() is the total indirect effect divided by that total. nie() still returns the chain-specific indirect effect by default. The new nie(x, type = "total") returns the total indirect effect, te(x) - nde(x). The serial lm/glm and lavaan extractors now record the skip-path coefficients as a2..ak (X -> Mj), b1..b{k-1} (Mi -> Y) and d{i}_{j} (Mi -> Mj, j > i + 1) in @estimates and @vcov. The delta-method SE of te in confint() and tidy() differentiates the full sum. It matches lavaan := SEs. Serial tidy() gains a nie_total row, glance() gains a nie_total column and coef(type = "effects") gains indirect_total, appended after total so existing positions are unchanged. A hand-built object whose predictor lists include a skip path without its coefficient gets NA and a warning from te() and pm(), because assuming zero would reproduce the bug. For glm fits with a non-identity link, the path sum is on the linear-predictor scale, as it already is for MediationData. quick() now prints the chain and total NIE side by side. Downstream impact: none for probmed (imports only extract_mediation()) or RMediation (its serial ci() reads @a_path, @d_path and @b_path, which are unchanged); neither calls serial te() or pm(). Code that stored serial te() or pm() values from medfit 0.4.0 or earlier will see different numbers.

  • tidy(<SerialMediationData>, type = "effects") no longer errors on mismatched row counts.

  • The single-mediator four-way decomposition (InteractionMediationData, lm/glm engine) now includes factor covariates in E[M | X = 0]. Covariate means were taken only for numeric data columns named after a coefficient, so a factor’s dummy coefficients (e.g. Gb, Gc) were skipped without a warning. NDE, INTref and the total effect were wrong, and so were their delta-method SEs. The means now come from the mediator model’s design matrix, as in JointMediationData, and both the point estimates and the gradients use them. Two other cases change for the same reason: transformed covariate terms (e.g. log(C), poly(C, 2)) were also skipped and are now included, and when a caller-supplied data has rows the mediator model did not use, the means now cover only the estimation sample. With case weights (e.g. fit_mediation(weights = )), the means are now weighted by them; they were unweighted before. Results with plain numeric covariates and no weights are unchanged. fit_mediation() with an X * M outcome formula is fixed as well. The lavaan engine accepts only numeric observed variables, so it is unaffected.

  • JointMediationData effect standard errors are no longer NA in tidy() and summary() when extract_mediation() receives data = and a model has a factor or transformed covariate (e.g. G with levels a/b/c, or poly(W, 2)); confint(parm = "effects") no longer errors for the same fits. The gradients rebuilt the covariate means from @data, which only works for a model frame, so the SE computation failed and tidy() and summary() caught the failure and reported NA. The extractor now stores the exact means the point estimate uses on @data (attribute medfit_covariate_means, the convention of the four-way extractor), so SEs with data = d equal those with data = NULL, including fits with subset =. Point estimates were already correct.

  • fit_mediation(se_type = "sandwich") now applies the sandwich estimator to fits with a treatment-by-mediator interaction. The four-way worker ignored vcov_fun and always used the model-based stats::vcov(), so the returned @vcov was identical to se_type = "model", with no warning. A vcov_fun passed to extract_mediation() now also reaches serial and parallel fits, which ignored it the same way.

  • The four-way decomposition now requires the identity link. A Gaussian glm() with another link (e.g. gaussian(link = "log")) passed the family check, and the linear four-way formulas were applied to a model that is not linear in its coefficients. It now errors, naming the link.

  • extract_mediation() now errors when m_star is supplied but no four-way decomposition or joint-effects fit uses it (no treatment-by-mediator term, or decomposition = "two_way"), on both the lm/glm and lavaan paths. The value was previously dropped silently. As in fit_mediation(), the check keys on whether m_star was given at the call site, not on its value.

  • extract_mediation() on lm/glm fits now detects products written inside a function call, such as I(X * M). R records such a term as an ordinary covariate, so it previously bypassed both the multi-mediator product guard and the single-mediator interaction check: the fit returned main-effect estimates that ignored the product, with no error. Multi-mediator extraction now errors on any wrapped term that combines the treatment or a mediator with another variable (e.g. I(X * M2) or log(M1 + C)). Single-mediator extraction errors on a wrapped treatment-by-mediator product and asks for X * M or X:M, which route to the four-way decomposition. Single-variable transforms such as I(X^2) are unaffected, and a product precomputed as a data column still cannot be detected from the formula.

  • confint(parm = "effects") for MediationData gave a total-effect interval that was too wide: it treated the indirect effect and c' as independent, dropping their covariance. It now uses the full delta-method gradient (on the simple mediation_demo fit the TE standard error drops from 0.127 to 0.119, matching a parametric bootstrap). NIE and NDE are unchanged.

  • confint(parm = "effects") and tidy() now work for MediationData extracted from lavaan. Both located paths by lm-style names, so confint() stopped with “Could not compute SEs for effects” and tidy() omitted standard errors.

  • extract_mediation() with two or more mediators (serial or parallel) now errors when a model carries a product term involving the treatment or a mediator, e.g. X:M1 in the outcome model. Previously the multi-mediator branch returned before any interaction check, so the product term was ignored silently and main-effect paths were reported as if no interaction existed. Applies to both the lm/glm and lavaan methods; for lavaan, a product precomputed as a plain data column is recognized when named via interaction =. Products among covariates alone are still allowed. On lm/glm, a treatment-by-mediator product in the outcome model is now supported through JointMediationData (see New features); every other product still errors.

  • extract_mediation() on a lavaan fit whose paths carry custom labels (e.g. M ~ aa*X) now fills the alias rows of @vcov (a, b, c_prime, and the serial, parallel, and interaction aliases) from the labeled parameters. Previously the label-based parameter names from lavaan did not match the names the extractors looked for, so those rows and columns were all zero, and bootstrap_mediation(method = "parametric") drew a degenerate distribution with a zero-width interval. The simple extractor only recognized labels equal to a_label/b_label/cp_label; the serial, parallel, and interaction extractors recognized no labels at all. All four now read each path’s parameter name from lavaan::parTable().
